input.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet HSE gives ~2.0 eV for Sb6O13 (mp-684679), which is below the 2.7 eV photon energy. Sb-rich mixed-valence Sb oxides are the most plausible visible absorbers. ZnSb2O6 and Zn7Sb2O12 also predict ~1.95 eV, but these are probably underestimates. ZnSb2O4 predicts 4.2 eV, so it is inactive. The prediction can't separate the compositions much, so I'm sampling the Sb-rich end first.

content.text:
I submitted **index 21 (Sb 0.89, Zn 0.11)** as the best composition. All 3 merit measurements are used, and every result is very low.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.89 | 0.0073 |
| 16 | 0.81 | 0.0032 |
| 6 | 0.40 | 0.0031 |

- **XRD didn't help.** I used 4 of the 5 XRD measurements, at Sb 0.25, 0.47, 0.64 and 0.89. All four show the same main peaks (Q ≈ 2.79, 4.55, 5.33 Å⁻¹), and none of the listed phases matches well (similarity below 0.3). I couldn't use it to find phase regions.
- **The band-gap predictions didn't separate the compositions.** MEGNet predicted gaps near 2 eV for most Sb–Zn oxides, 4.2 eV for ZnSb₂O₄, and near 0 eV for two predicted-only phases, ZnSb₄O₉ and Zn₃Sb₂O₇. I measured at both near-zero-gap compositions (indices 16 and 6), and both gave less than half the EQE of index 21.
- **Gaps in coverage:** 23 of the 26 compositions were never measured. That includes the Zn-rich end (Sb below 0.40), the region around ZnSb₂O₆ (Sb 0.64–0.76) and the most Sb-rich films (indices 22–25). With three points, I can't tell whether index 21 is near the library's best or just the best of a weak sample.
